2024_180_june_2024_ac_plan_boe_presentat.paragraph: Board of Education presentation titled "Project 2026 Blueprint," delivered to the Troy School District board on June 6, 2024, reporting the district Accountability Plan against the four "World Class for All" pillars. Each pillar objective is reported in a uniform format of Objectives, Key Results, and Challenges and Recommendations, covering Deep Learning (Blue Pillar), Building Capacity (Gold Pillar), Equity and Well-Being (Red Pillar), and Early Childhood to Career (Green Pillar). The most concrete outcome reported is the personalized transition of 326 students into Troy School District kindergarten, alongside an increase in GSRP slots for 2024-25.
2024_180_june_2024_ac_plan_boe_presentat.page:
**What this is**
Slide deck presented to the Troy School District Board of Education on June 6, 2024, branded "Project 2026 Blueprint" and "Troy School District." It presents the district ACCOUNTABILITY PLAN, stating that the "World Class for All" Pillars hold the team accountable to Objectives, Key Results, and Challenges and Recommendations.

**Pillar framework**

| Pillar | Color | Objectives reported |
|---|---|---|
| Deep Learning | Blue | 4 |
| Building Capacity | Gold | 3 |
| Equity and Well-Being | Red | 2 |
| Early Childhood to Career | Green | 2 |

**Deep Learning (Blue Pillar)**
Objective 1 is to create and sustain systems of support at all levels that deepen learning and empower student voice (MTSS), asserting that access to deep learning is imperative for all children. Key results cite partnership and learning with New Solutions K-12 (student supports K-12), Solution Tree (PLC model 6-12), and Oakland Schools (MTSS). Challenges for elementary and secondary MTSS are to continue monitoring benchmark data, continue developing capacity in math, and solidify tier-one instruction in all classrooms. Objective 2 addresses improving technology access for students and families with quality training; items listed include development of an Artificial Intelligence leadership committee, development of a computer science leadership team, continuing to grow digital portfolios for students to document learning over time, and building understanding of meaningful use of AI in the classroom. Objective 3 is to continue pursuing global best practices in all content areas (NPDL, The 6 C's, learning partnerships), with key results of Solution Tree Professional Learning Communities K-12, NSK12 Supporting All Students, hosting the Midwest Literacy Institute, and Math Recovery K-12. Objective 4 is to take action for upgraded facilities, referencing Fielding International comprehensive guiding principles for MS and HS Redesign, involvement of all stakeholders in the design process, ongoing staff learning tied to curriculum, ongoing bond project work, and supporting vision and implementation efforts.

**Building Capacity (Gold Pillar)**
Objective 1 covers improving educator preparation, strengthening pipelines for underrepresented educators, and supporting current educators: attending university job fairs, "Grow Your Own" programs, hosting job fairs for educators, employee support groups, a leadership cohort, and a New Teacher Learning Series. Challenges named are teacher shortage and limited university education enrollment. Objective 2 covers job-embedded professional learning for all staff, use of release days to prioritize conversations with collaborative teacher teams, emerging professional learning communities, and building systemness with counseling 6-12 around program opportunities. Objective 3 covers professional learning for staff, community, and students to co-design impactful experiences for the OneTroy community, citing continued partnership with Celebrate Hope, community engagement (Community Book Read and Experience Panel), building student capacity through WEB, LEAP and a Student Leadership Conference, and Learning Nights at all schools for parents and community.

**Equity and Well-Being (Red Pillar)**
Objective 1 is to fund additional investments supporting the needs of the whole child, listing SEL curriculum and programming, a Behavioral Threat Assessment (BTA) committee, community engagement, SEL curriculum and program implementation, PLC collaborative work, and district training on a new BTA tool. Objective 2 elevates focus on Alignment, Access, and Agency district wide, with a Belonging Survey, Student Equity Council expansion, an inclusive calendar built with community input, restorative practices (train all administrators, grow building cohorts), equity teamwork across buildings, and "Belonging as a System." A closing slide is headed "Red Pillar: January - June 2024."

**Early Childhood to Career (Green Pillar)**
Objective 1 continues investment in high-quality early childhood education and advocacy for universal preschool for all three- and four-year-olds; key results are increased GSRP slots for 2024-25, personalized transition of 326 students to TSD Kindergarten, and continued connection to TSD K-5 curriculum. Challenges are recruitment and retention of highly qualified staff and preparation for universal preschool. Objective 2 expands college and career pathways for middle and high school students, listing the 99b Computer Science / Computational Thinking Grant, Early Middle College with LTU, a Career Accelerator Program, 8th grade interviews and portfolio, and a computer science elective at all 4 middle school buildings.
2024_180_june_2024_ac_plan_boe_presentat.verbose:
Presentation slides delivered to the Troy School District Board of Education at its meeting of June 6, 2024, under the cover title "Project 2026 Blueprint" with the district branding "Troy School District." The deck presents the district ACCOUNTABILITY PLAN and states that the "World Class for All" Pillars hold the team accountable to three reporting elements: Objectives, Key Results, and Challenges and Recommendations. Four color-coded pillars organize the presentation - Blue (Deep Learning), Gold (Building Capacity), Red (Equity and Well-Being), and Green (Early Childhood to Career) - and the pillar slides carry the running header "Key Results & Objectives June 2024."

DEEP LEARNING - BLUE PILLAR

Objective 1: "Create and sustain systems of support at all levels that deepen learning and empower student voice (MTSS). Access to deep learning is imperative for all children." Key results are partnership and learning with New Solutions K-12 (student supports K-12); partnership and learning with Solution Tree (PLC model 6-12); and partnership and learning with Oakland Schools (MTSS). Challenges and recommendations, listed under "Elementary & Secondary MTSS," are to continue to monitor benchmark data, continue to develop capacity in math, and solidify tier-one instruction in all classrooms.

Objective 2: "Improve technology access for students and families while providing quality training to leverage the use of technology to deepen learning." The items reported on this slide are development of an Artificial Intelligence leadership committee, development of a computer science leadership team, continuing to grow digital portfolios for students to document learning over time, and building understanding of meaningful use of AI in the classroom.

Objective 3: "Continue to pursue the global best practices of all content areas (NPDL, The 6 C's, Learning partnerships)." Key results are Solution Tree: Professional Learning Communities K-12; NSK12: Supporting All Students; host of the Midwest Literacy Institute; and Math Recovery K-12. The challenge and recommendation is to continue to build cohesion within content areas through professional learning communities.

Objective 4: "Take action for upgraded facilities to meet the demands of a world-class learning environment in all school communities." The reported items are Fielding International comprehensive guiding principles for MS and HS Redesign, involvement of all stakeholders in the design process for school environments, ongoing staff learning opportunities with connection to curriculum, ongoing bond project work, and supporting vision and implementation efforts.

BUILDING CAPACITY - GOLD PILLAR

Objective 1: "Improving educator preparation, strengthening pipelines for underrepresented educators, and supporting current educators." Key results are attending university job fairs; utilizing "Grow Your Own" programs; hosting job fairs for educators; employee support groups; a leadership cohort; and a New Teacher Learning Series. Challenges and recommendations are the teacher shortage and challenges with limited university education enrollment.

Objective 2: "Continue to provide job-embedded professional learning experiences for all staff." Key results are job-embedded learning for staff and utilizing release days to prioritize conversations with collaborative teacher teams around student learning, with emerging professional learning communities. The challenge and recommendation is to build systemness with counseling 6-12 around program opportunities.

Objective 3: "Provide professional learning opportunities for learning for staff, community, and students with the goal of co-designing impactful experiences to better the OneTroy community." Key results are continued partnership with Celebrate Hope; community engagement through the Community Book Read and Experience Panel; building student capacity via WEB, LEAP, and a Student Leadership Conference; and Learning Nights at all schools for parents and community. The challenge and recommendation is to continue community book reads and call to action.

EQUITY AND WELL-BEING - RED PILLAR

Objective 1: "Fund additional investments to support the needs of the whole child." The reported items are SEL curriculum and program implementation, PLC collaborative work, district training on the new BTA tool, SEL curriculum and programming, a Behavioral Threat Assessment (BTA) committee, and community engagement through the Community Book Read and Experience Panel, framed by the recommendation to continue to invest in opportunities to grow meaningful relationships in all buildings.

Objective 2: "Elevate focus on Alignment, Access, and Agency district wide." Key results are elevating student experience through a Belonging Survey and Student Equity Council expansion, and building an inclusive calendar with community input. Challenges and recommendations are community engagement and partnerships; a structure for intentional collaboration and connection; encouraging and implementing aligned structures; equity teamwork across buildings; restorative practices, specifically training all administrators and growing building cohorts; and "Belonging as a System," described as an inclusive newsletter, data culture, professional learning, and resources for honoring diversity - thought and being - as embedded practices. A further Red Pillar slide is headed "January - June 2024."

EARLY CHILDHOOD TO CAREER - GREEN PILLAR

Objective 1: "Continue to invest in high-quality early childhood education, including advocating for access to universal preschool for all three and four-year-olds." Key results are personalized transition of 326 students to TSD Kindergarten, continued connection to TSD K-5 curriculum, and increased GSRP slots for 2024-25. Challenges and opportunities are recruitment and retention of highly qualified staff and preparation for universal preschool (expanding access).

Objective 2: "Expand college and career pathways for middle and high school students." The stated aim is to provide more students with access to high-quality career and technical education programs that expand access to computer science; connect underrepresented students to careers in demand in high-growth industry sectors; and build partnerships with institutions of higher education, employers, and other stakeholders that allow students to engage in quality, work-based learning opportunities, earn a credential, and/or earn college credit. Key results are Portrait of a Learner in student portfolios; career readiness engagement opportunities K-8 partnered with media specialists and Maker Space; the 99b Computer Science / Computational Thinking Grant; K-12 CS alignment with Oakland Schools and MDE; expanded maker-centered learning spaces to the high school level; Early Middle College with LTU; a Career Accelerator Program; 8th grade interviews and portfolio; and a computer science elective at all 4 middle school buildings. Challenges and opportunities are supporting secondary building leaders to embed career readiness initiatives in classrooms and beyond; Portrait of a Learner, leveraging and embracing connection to the current strategic plan; prioritizing digital citizenship for K-12; and growing and developing computer science in the K-12 curriculum.

The deck closes on the same "Project 2026 Blueprint" / Troy School District title treatment with which it opens. No dollar amounts, budget figures, votes, or contract awards are contained in the presentation; the only enumerated figures are the 326 students transitioned to TSD Kindergarten, the 4 middle school buildings offering the computer science elective, the 99b grant designation, and the 2024-25 school year reference for expanded GSRP slots.
